Patterns

A component is one brick: a card, a button, a row panel. A pattern is a fixed composition of bricks that already repeats on the screens: the frame of a pushed screen, the whole-screen message, a list of cards under its label. Each one below is built only from components on the components page, carries no CSS and no class of its own, and is copied from a real screen. The source of each is one file in design-system/patterns/.

A pattern exists only where it already stands on three screens. The build holds that rule: every screen a pattern names must exist in wireframes/ and still carry the classes the pattern is made of, and the names must add up to three screens once a screen's -empty, -error, -loading and service files are counted as that one screen. When a screen stops carrying a pattern, the build fails until the pattern or the screen is put right. A composition found on one or two screens stays in those screens and is not drawn here.

Take the pattern when

  • The new screen does a job an existing screen already does. Arrived from elsewhere and ends in a decision: Pushed screen. One of the four tabs: Tab root. Nothing to show: Whole-screen message. Take the pattern's markup, keep its order, its zone labels and where its actions go, and change only the words and the data.
  • You would otherwise choose the order of parts yourself. The pattern has already settled it: outcome before record, label before panel, the primary above the secondaries, the exit inside the message or in the action bar but never both.

Build from components when

  • No pattern does the screen's job. Build it from the components, and if the same composition then reaches three screens it becomes a pattern here.
  • Only part of the screen changes. One zone failing is a Message block in that zone, not a whole-screen message; one fact is a note, not a panel.
  • The pattern almost fits. Do not bend a pattern with a modifier or an inline style. A pattern has no CSS to bend; a change of look is a change to a component, made in design-system/components/ and shown on every screen that uses it.

Looked for and not found

Three compositions were looked for and stand on fewer than three screens, so they are not patterns:

  • A list header with a filter. The finder with its filter drawer stands on listings only; the in-page tabs over a list stand on operator-listings and time-slot. Two screens.
  • The search home. It is one screen, and it is the Finder component.
  • The call. It stands on three screens but is one component, the Call surface.

From order-details.

  • .dr-statusbar — the iOS status bar, drawn, owned by nothing.
  • .dr-topbar with .dr-back — the chevron alone, named Back to {destination} for assistive tech, and the screen's one title. No brand, no second control.
  • .dr-main — labelled zones, one section heading above each.
  • .dr-actionbar — the decision. The primary on top, secondaries under it (rev 290).

Take the pattern

The user arrives from another screen and the screen ends in an action: pay, confirm, send, save. Take the frame whole and change only what is inside main.

Build from components instead

The screen is one of the four tab destinations (take Tab root), or it has no nav bar at all, like the call (take Call surface). A pushed screen with nothing to commit drops the action bar and keeps the rest: earning-details, notifications and operator-notifications are built that way.

Tab root

One of the four places the tab bar leads to. It has no back, because nothing is behind it.

From wallet.

Take the pattern

The screen is a tab destination. Its action, if it has one, goes in the floating capsule or inside main, because the tab bar holds the bottom. tracking is the one tab screen that trades the tab bar for an action bar while an order is live, and its -empty and -error files keep the tab bar.

Build from components instead

listings and operator-listings are tab roots too, but they put the notification bell or the operator's own head in the title's place: build those from the Screen shell parts and the Finder.

Whole-screen message

The screen's content is missing or failed, so main holds one zone label and one message, and the frame around it stays exactly as it was.

Built from: Message block · Banner message · Section heading · the screen's own frame

When the screen already has an action bar, the exits stay there (Try again on top) and the message carries none of its own.

From payment-error.

Take the pattern

The whole screen has nothing to show: an empty list, a failed load, a declined payment. One message, one way out, nothing else in main.

Build from components instead

Only one zone fails and the rest of the screen still holds: tracking-error keeps the map, the rail and the rows, and the message is one zone among them. Use the Message block alone there.

From resolution.

  • .dr-center — the Outcome: the milestone mark, the fact as a display line, one lead line.
  • .dr-label + .dr-rows — the record, key and value, labelled like any other zone.
  • The next step: in the action bar (resolution, inspection-report) or as a block button closing main on a tab root (order-confirmed).

Take the pattern

A job, an order or a case reached its end and the user needs both the fact and the receipt. order-confirmed puts the operator card and inspection-report the report before the rows; the order is outcome first, record after.

Build from components instead

The result is still on its way: take Waiting outcome. A finished thing with no record to show needs only the Outcome.

Waiting outcome

Something is being handed off and will come back: a provider sign-in, a payment, a withdrawal. The screen names what is happening and holds the place for the answer.

Built from: Outcome · Skeleton · Action bar

Take the pattern

The wait is for another party: Diia, Bank ID, Apple Pay, the bank. Nothing on the screen can be shown yet.

Build from components instead

A list or a detail screen is loading its own data: keep the screen's layout and put Skeleton bars where the content goes (order-history-loading, inspection-report-loading).
